utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Muireann Dennehy on behalf of the Prosecution along with my colleague Matthew Olmsted, Thomas Laugel, and our intern Matija Saftic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic, lead counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The next ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The next witness is 101?

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Before we do that, there is an exhibit issue. Mr. Zivanovic, your Exhibit Number D5, you asked for -- to tender a new translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And there was no objection from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So we will admit it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And before we bring the witness in, I noticed that we got three exhibit lists for this witness, three in a row, each one updated in some way or another. Can I suggest to the OTP that when we have such follow-up exhibit lists that you indicate on the list what is new and what is left out, because if not, we're completely lost and we have to check every -- every single document. And it would also be very helpful for everybody if you could indicate, if that's the case, that there are documents on the list that are not yet on your 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: We will do, Your Honour, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The witness may be brought in. Closed session, please, to bring the witness in.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You have protective measures, ma'am, which means in your case that we will not -- we will not call you by your name but by your pseudonym, and you have face distortion as well. I will ask you to read the solemn declaration. Before I do that, I must tell you that -- that you expose yourself to the penalties of perjury should you give untruthful or misleading information to the Tribunal. Can you please give the solemn declaration now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Dennehy, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can I ask you whether you can hear me in a language that you understand.

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Dennehy, I realise that I forgot the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Yes. I was just to come to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: May I ask that 65 ter 6381 be shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Without reading anything out loud on at that document, can you please affirm that the information on that document is correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask that this document, 65 ter 6381, be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1001. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And may I ask that that also be admitted under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell the Court where you live.

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: In Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how long have you lived --

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: In Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how long have you lived in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Thirty years.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I appear to have a problem with my translation. Do you mind if I speak to my Case Manager quickly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Why did you first move to Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I found a job there.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And did -- did your husband move to Erdut with you at that time?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And -- and why did he move to Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Also for work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Dennehy, we are in open session. Do you realise that?

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Yes. If we could go into closed session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Closed session, please -- private session, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: When did the ZNG move into the centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Sometime around the 28th of April, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And why did the ZNG move into the centre in April 1991?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Because -- or, rather, in order to defend the territory of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And why was it necessary that the ZNG move into the centre then? Why was it necessary at that time to defend the territory of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The local Serbs had erected barricades. There was an uprisal [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you describe where the barricades were erected?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: In front of Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Were there barricades elsewhere around Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: After that, on Bijelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did you react to the barricades in Bijelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I found it very hard.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Why did you find it very hard?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: We could not communicate with Osijek. We could not go to Osijek either.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what other effects of the tensions did you see or know about at that time?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: An armed rebellion started.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what did that mean for you in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The beginning of war.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What happened to your employment in July 1991?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I was fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And -- and why were you fired?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Because of my ethnicity. I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you please describe to us what happened at the Vodovod plant near Erdut at the end of July 1991.

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: It was shelled.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you describe the shelling to the Court.

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: During the night, after 1.00 a.m., until 4.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what did you hear between 1.00 a.m. and 4.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Terrible shelling, and there was a strong light, although it was during the night.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who was causing the shelling?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And where were they shelling from?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: From Vojvodina in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you describe the damage that resulted as a cause of the attack?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Seven houses were damaged in Erdut. They were shelled. And the waterworks, the water plant, was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Where were you at the time of the attack?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: In my own house.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did you feel at the time that the attack was occurring?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Frightened.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What military presence was there in Erdut following the attack on the Vodovod?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What army was in Erdut after the attack on the Vodovod?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The ZNG.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And was there any other army there?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Prior to the attack on the Vodovod, did you see any JNA representative in the village of Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you tell me about the time that you saw a JNA representative in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They arrived in a jeep. They reached the centre of the village to inform the local commune representatives that the JNA troops on the Danube should not be provoked. If there were provocations, they would raze Erdut to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: You just told us that they arrived in a jeep. Who arrived in a jeep?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: A JNA officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And why did he say that the JNA troops on the Danube should not be provoked?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Because a soldier was hit from the Erdut tower. He was in a patrol boat, and the bullet hit the helmet on his head.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And when the JNA officer told you that if there were further provocations they would raze Erdut to the ground, what do you take this to mean?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: That all of us in the village would die.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did that make you feel?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Miserable and frightened.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: After the attack on the Vodovod, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I went to Vojvodina, to Indjija.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And why did you leave Erdut to go to Indjija?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: For the safety of my children. I stayed with my cousin.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: When did you return to Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: In the month of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And in August when you returned, who had taken charge of the village of Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence, the local Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And when you arrived back in August to Erdut, how were Croats in Erdut reacting to the attack on the Vodovod and the further attacks?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They were horrified.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And where did they go?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They went across Aljmas to Osijek after the attack on Vodovod. They didn't want to stay in the village. They went on a barge.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And why did they not want to stay in the village?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They were afraid for their own safety. They wanted to save themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And why were they afraid for their own safety? Who were they afraid of?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They were afraid of the army and the local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what army were they afraid of?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And was the work paid or was this a work obligation?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: It was a work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what did you receive as payment for this work?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: We did not get paid.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I ask that we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: When you returned to work at the training centre, who did you expect to arrive there?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The local Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And -- and did the local Territorial Defence arrive at the centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who else later arrived at the centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And when did Arkan arrive at the centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: 20th -- no, sorry, 26th September.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And before the 26th of September when Arkan arrived, did anyone else -- or was any other group present at the centre at the time?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Mr. Badza.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who was Badza?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: State security of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what was his role at the centre? What did he do?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was with his men, but I don't know what his role was.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Was he in charge of those men? Was he in a position of authority?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What did his men call him, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Mr. Badza.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And do you know Badza's full name?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Radovan Stojicic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how often would you see Badza yourself at the centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: During lunch, breakfast, and dinner.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Now, moving on to when Arkan arrived, you said earlier that he arrived on the 26th of September, 1991. What was the reaction of those at the centre to Arkan's arrival?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Disapproval.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And why did they disapprove of him being there?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Because he had been driven away by the locals of Tenja village.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what did he done in Tenja to be driven away?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He imposed his own command.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Who accompanied Arkan when he arrived at the centre? Who else did you see with him?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Twenty-five of his soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what was your impression of these men?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They were frightening.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Why do you think -- or why were you frightened at the time, or why did you consider them frightening?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They looked arrogant, Rambo-like soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And where were these men from, these 25 soldiers who accompanied Arkan?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: From Serbia, and some from Croatian territories.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And were these ordinary soldiers who accompanied Arkan to the centre in September?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What rank do you think these soldiers held?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: His helpers, officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Court when you first met Arkan?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I was intimidated.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And when did you first meet him?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: When he entered the kitchen and arrogantly introduced himself as the commander of the Serb Volunteers Guard, and from now on we would be working as he orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what did you understand the Serb Volunteer Guard to be?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The elite guard made up of Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what did Arkan say he intended to do at the camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: To train elite units of the Serb Volunteers Guard.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you describe the weapons and the military equipment that Arkan's officers brought with them?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Modern.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what kind of modern equipment did they have?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Beginning with Skorpion pistols, machine-guns, modern machine-guns, to all the other weapons that we had no occasion to see before.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did you react when you saw these weapons?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Frightened.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And why were you frightened?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Because of the way they behaved.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did they behave?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Arrogant and supercilious.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what kind of uniforms did Arkan's men wear?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: First it was olive green-black uniforms and camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what kind of vehicles did they have at the camp, what kind of vehicles?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Jeeps and armoured vans.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what registration plates did these vehicles have?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Belgrade licence plates.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Now, you told us earlier that Arkan arrived with a number of officers and that his intentions were to train the Serb Volunteer Guard at the camp. Did the number of soldiers at the camp increase over time?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how many men were at the camp over time?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Over 200 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And as the number of men increased at the camp, did additional weaponry arrive?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Where did this weaponry come from?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And can you describe that weaponry for me?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Kalashnikovs.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Was there anything else?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Launchers, RPGs, grenades.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Now, moving on to your time in the kitchen at the camp, how did the food at the camp differ after Arkan's arrival?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: How did -- what types of food did you have after Arkan's arrival at the camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Beef, chicken, and pork.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And was the food different after Arkan had arrived at the camp compared to before?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: In the early days there was less of it, and later it was a richer diet.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And can you describe why -- or can you tell us why it was a richer diet?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Because he brought food for his men.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what kind of food did Arkan bring for his men?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Juice, chocolate, steak, prosciutto, all sorts of cheese.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And could you and other villagers in Erdut buy similar food at the time?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And where did the food that you've described such as juice and chocolate, where did that come from?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: From Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Where did Arkan get the money to purchase such food?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I ask that we move into private session, please, and can I also ask that the previous answer be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes. Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: If I can repeat the last question to you, Witness. Do you know of other Croats who were beaten by Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who were those other Croats?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Marijan Simunovic, Ivan Jakob, and a few other villagers.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I now ask that 65 ter 4802.3 at tab 12 be shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the photograph in front of you? Do you --

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Do you recognise the man in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Who is this man?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Milorad Stricevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I please ask that this document be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record, this document is already admitted into evidence as Exhibit P9. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, what was Milorad Stricevic's relationship with Arkan?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was his colonel.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And were there other colonels that Arkan had in his men?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you name those colonels for me, please?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Colonel Peja, Milorad Ulemek.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I now please ask that 65 ter 4762, that's at tab 5, be shown. This is a video-clip, and the relevant parts are at 42.3, that's 42 minutes, 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, on the screen in front of you, do you recognise any of these men?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Who are these men?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Arkan's officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you name any of these men for me?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The first on the right is Suco. Next to him is Bojke, and then Jova, and finally Kaljavi.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And the first individual who you named, is this the man who beat your husband?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can the record please show that the witness has identified the individual at 43.19 of this video as the individual Suco, the man who beat her husband.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I think the record shows.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the other images in this video?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: This is in the Erdut Training Centre where he trained the Serbian Volunteer Guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Where who trained the Volunteer Guards?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Arkan and his officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And the lineup that you've just seen in the video, was that usual to see Arkan's men in such a formation?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I please ask that this video be tendered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Dennehy, would this be 4762 or 4762.3, because that's the video -- or the CD the Registrar has.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That will be .3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Point 3, okay. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1002. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What did your husband do after he was beaten by Arkan and his men -- or excuse me, let me rephrase it. What did your husband do after he was beaten by Stricevic and Suco?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He requested protection from the local police.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who at the local police did he seek protection from?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: From Bozidar Bolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who was Bolic?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The police commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did Bolic react to your husband's request for protection?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He said he could not protect him. The only thing for him to do was to go across the river to Vojvodina. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And why did Bolic say that he could not protect your husband?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Where did your husband then go?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: A villager drove him in the direction of Bobota towards the active command of the JNA of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what did your husband do at Bobota?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was a member of the reserve JNA strength. That's what they gave him to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how many days after his beating did your husband leave for Bobota?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: On the third day.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And were you harassed by Arkan's men when they realised that your husband had joined the reserves?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did they harass you?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: One morning, two Arkan's soldiers came to my house. We were still asleep, I, my mother, and my three children. They ordered us to gather in the hallway, and they asked me where my husband, the Ustasha, was.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: How did you feel when they gathered you and your three children and they called your husband an Ustasha?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: It was very bad, terrible.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I just confirm one of your earlier replies. I asked you what did your husband do at Bobota, and you said that he joined the reserve JNA. Can you please confirm what -- what reserve force did your husband join?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The reserve force of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I ask that 65 ter 4789 be shown. That's at tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the room in this video?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I don't have anything on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And where is this room?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: In the centre where he trained his men.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And did you work in this room?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Not in this room but in the kitchen next to this room.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And do you recognise the individual in the video?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Who is this individual?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And do you recognise the animal in the video?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: A little tiger.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And did this tiger live at the training centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I please ask that this video, that's 65 ter 4789.1, be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1003. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I now ask that exhibit 65 ter 873, that's at tab 3, be shown. I apologise, it's 00873. Can we please go to page 2, scroll down to page 2 of that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, at page 2 of the document, I'd like to draw your attention to the line that says: "Food is of very good quality and well varied ... there are reportedly unlimited supplies of chocolate and juices." In your opinion, was there well varied food available at the camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Now, if we can please go to page 7 of this document. That's English page 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, if I can draw your attention to number 2 where the document states: "Building number 2: A cinema auditorium with 182 seats, a canteen with high-standing tables ..." And further down: "A kitchen with the latest kitchen equipment, meal preparation area with equipment, dining-room with 100-seat capacity and hot service counter." From your experience at the training centre, does this information accurately reflect the equipment that was available at the centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And the cinema auditorium with 182 seats, was this a room at the training centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And if you see at number 4, at the same page, where it notes: "A storage area with two rooms for storing weapons and ammunition ..." From your knowledge of the centre grounds, was there a storage area for storing weapons and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I please ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1004. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, I would now like to speak to you about the camp and the discipline at the camp. Can you please describe the discipline regime imposed by Arkan at the training camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was very strict.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: How did you know he was very strict?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He did not allow people to drink alcoholic drinks, and the attitude towards the soldiers was very strict.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did Arkan's soldiers behave as a result of the regime, the strict regime?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They were pretty disciplined.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: How did Arkan react to misbehaviour by his soldiers?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He punished them by tying them to a tree and beating them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Did he punish them by tying them to a tree and beat the soldiers himself? Did he himself do the beating?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No, his officers did.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you describe an incident where you saw soldiers being beaten for misbehaviour?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes. He was tied to a tree in front of the kitchen. Two of his officers were beating him with police batons. You know those are sticks that we call police batons.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who was tied to a tree?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: One of his soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what happened after the officers had finished beating him with the police batons?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He fainted. They poured water over him, and they took him to their prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what had this soldier done in order to be punished in this way?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He had been drinking.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note the time and wonder whether now might be an appropriate time to rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Dennehy. Witness, we will take our first break. We will come back at 11.00. The court usher will escort you out of court. Thank you. Just one moment, please. Mr. Usher, just one moment. Closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, before the break we -- you spoke about the manner in which Arkan used to punish his men. Did any of Arkan's men ever try to escape from the training camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you describe an incident that you know of when one of Arkan's men escaped from the camp or attempted to escape from the camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: His name was Neso. He was from Serbia, from a town called Smederevska Palanka, a young boy. He realised that the centre was not his place, and he tried to escape, but Arkan's soldiers caught him and took him back to the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what happened when Arkan's soldiers caught him and brought him back to the centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They dressed him in the old Yugoslav uniform, and he was punished by chores such as collecting rubbish over the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Did Neso attempt to escape the camp after the first time?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes, he did. And on his second try, the soldiers caught him but he did not come back to the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What do you think happened to him?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They killed him.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Did anyone inquire about his whereabouts after his disappearance?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: His parents came to visit him. They were received by Colonel Savo, who told them that he was killed in combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Was there any investigation into his disappearance?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I ask that 65 ter 4765.1, that's at tab 6, be shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the scenes in the video?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: It was the compound of the centre. The assembly of his guard with a trumpet.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And do you recognise the individual playing the trumpet?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Who is that individual?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: One of his soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Do you recognise the flag that is flying in the video?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The Serbian flag.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask that this video be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1005. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, who were the foreign dignitaries who visited Arkan at the training centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Mr. Zhirinovski, Vladimir Zhirinovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Was there anyone else who visited Arkan?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The minister of Krajina, Mr. Mrgud.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Mrgud's full name?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: His last name was Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Zhirinovski visited Arkan. Where was Mr. Zhirinovski from?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Russia.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who was Vladimir Zhirinovski?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I think he was a politician.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did Arkan treat the visit of Vladimir Zhirinovski?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: It was a great honour. He treated him also with honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And can you describe what those honours involved?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The whole guard was assembled and a welcome party was organised within the compound.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And did any other foreigners visit Arkan at the training centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: There was a representative from Greece.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Do you know whether this representative from Greece was a government representative?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: It was said he was a politician.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Was there any foreign media or journalists at the camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: There was a gentleman who spoke English, and he filmed the drills of the guard with his camera, and there was a young man accompanying him wearing a Scottish kilt.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Now, going back to late 1991, when you were at home ill at that time, who did you see, at your home, being taken away by Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: From my own house I saw Arkan's men leading local men whose hands were tied with chains, or they were handcuffed in groups of two or three. They were taken by Arkan's men to the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And do you know who these men were? Did you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The first one to be taken in was Mr. Vidoje Sutalo, then Stjepan Cakvari, Franjo Piholj [as interpreted], and Andrija Matin.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Now, you said that you could see the local men whose hands were tied with chains. Can you describe what the chains looked like?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Thin chains. Their hands were tied in the back, and the chain, the other end of the chain was held by a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And the men who you saw and who you've named, what ethnicity were those men?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Mr. Vidoje Sutalo was a Croat. Mr. Stjepan Cakvari was Hungarian. Andrija Matin, Croat, and Franjo Piholj, Croat.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And where did Arkan's men take those men who you've named?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The prison within the compound.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did Arkan's men treat the detainees during their detention at the camp in the prison?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I don't know, because I have never been inside in the centre. I always stayed at my own home.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Were there other prisoners detained in the camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you describe who those prisoners were?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: There were Hungarians.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how many Hungarians were held as prisoner at the camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Fifteen to 20 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And where were they detained in the camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: In that prison within the compound of the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And was there anything unusual about where the Hungarians were kept?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes. Those used to be public restrooms converted into a prison, a very cramped space.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did Arkan's men treat the Hungarian prisoners? What did they make them do?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They kicked the iron door and made them sing the Serbian anthem.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And when you were working in the kitchen, did you cook for those detainees?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Were they given food while they were detained at the centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Do you know if any of the other cooks cooked food for the detainees?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how long were the Hungarian men detained for at the training centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Around eight days.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They were taken away. I don't know what they became.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And where are they now?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They're all dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, you named a number of men whom you saw from your own home, and I'd just like to confirm one of the names. You mentioned Franjo Pihtl. Is that correct? Can you please repeat the person's name?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Franjo Pihtl, P-i-h-t-l.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall seeing female prisoners at the camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I saw two women, one younger, under 35, and one older woman, 65, around 65.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And can you describe how the older woman looked when you saw her detained at the camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: She was escorted by the soldiers across the yard. She was wearing a gown and slippers.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What do you mean by "gown"?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The robe, the kind you put on when you get up in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And in relation to the Hungarian men who were detained at the prison, do you recall any of their names?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you tell me their names?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Bence, Mr. Bence. Then Nikola Kalozi, and two other men named Kalozi. I can't recall their first names now.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And other than the Hungarian men and the women who you've described, do you know of anyone else who was detained at the centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: A local man, Albert Djuro, Helena Albert, Antun Zubovic, Antun Moskovic, Viktorija Albert, Ana Terzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what happened to those people who you've just named?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They were all killed during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Do you know or did you know Marinko Simunovic?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was also detained. He was beaten up at the centre, at the prison there, and later at his home already he succumbed to the injuries he sustained during the beating.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: You say that he succumbed to his injuries. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Since he was beaten up there, he was released to go home, and he died at his home.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Did you know a woman or know of a woman called Manda Maj?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What happened to Manda?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The local police took her away by night and she was also killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who took her away?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Two policemen from the local police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I ask that 65 ter 6254 now be shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Do you recognise what this photograph represents?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What is the image in front of us?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: You can see the centre where Arkan trained his guard; the winery, the wine factory; and the chateau inside the winery.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you take the pen in front of you and draw a circle around the area that you call Arkan's camp.

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you write the number 1 next to that, please.

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, can you now draw a circle around your house and write the number 2 next to it.

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Dennehy, should we go into closed session for this?

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Closed session, please -- private session, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, you've just testified that you saw Mr. Hadzic at the camp around a dozen times. Why was Mr. Hadzic at the camp, at the training camp?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Who did he visit there?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And you said that Mr. Hadzic resided at the Dvorac. Can you please describe what that building was?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: It was an apartment where he usually stayed in the castle.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And why did Mr. Hadzic stay in the castle?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What position did Mr. Hadzic hold at the time?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was the president of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Hadzic hold meetings at the castle?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what kind of meetings were those?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Political.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Who attended those meetings?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: People from the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I please ask that 65 ter 4879.1 be shown.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] ... question mark whether the Serb region is to stay within Croatia. Serb people do not accept that because they want to be within --"

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can we please play the video-clip again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] He was satisfied with the present course of discussions and that a step forward had been made. It is still under question mark whether the Serb region is to stay within Croatia. The Serb people do not accept that because they want to be within ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the room in the video?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: It is a room in the castle.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who was the main speaker in the video?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And what used to take place in this room in the castle?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Meetings took place there, the meetings of the government of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I please ask that this 65 ter 4879.1 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Dennehy, the Registrar tells me that the transcript is uploaded -- sorry, isn't uploaded yet. Shall we mark it for identification?

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Registrar, pending the upload of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1007, marked for identification pending upload of the transcript and the translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I now ask that 65 ter 4879.2 be shown.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Those are Communist borders. Borders have already been moved, external and internal ones, both. Krajina spoke out and you know our big National Assembly's decision disrupted its legal continuity with the Republic of Croatia. So the borders are as they are, and I'm in favour of not changing them. Leave them as they are. This means ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I ask that the video-clip be replayed and frozen at the outset, the first -- 13.04.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Those are Communist borders."

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, I've now shown you another video-clip. Do you recognise the room, again, in this video-clip?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Is this the same room as before?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who do you recognise as the individual on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And can you confirm again where this meeting is taking place?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: In the castle's conference hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: May I ask that this video-clip be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked. The same problem.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1008, marked for identification pending upload of the translation and the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: May I ask that 65 ter 4809.5 now be shown.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] I hope that regarding the ongoing acceptance of the amendments as proposed by Presidents Milosevic and Bulatovic, if they will be accepted, and I'm not sure if he had accepted them, they would mean a step forward. However, what I'm saying is that this can be only the first step forward, but the final decision for our problem can be reached only through the United Nations."

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I ask that this be shown again and it frozen at the outset. And it --

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the room in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And where is this room?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: In the castle.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who is the main speaker in this video-clip?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Mr. Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I please ask that this video-clip be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1009, marked for identification pending upload of the transcript and translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned that Mr. Hadzic held government meetings at the castle, at the Dvorac. Do you know who attended those meetings? Do you know anyone in particular who attended?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Mr. Minister whose nickname was Mrgud.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And do you recall Mrgud's full name?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Milutinovic, but I don't know the first name.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Were there any other Krajina government officials who you saw in Erdut at these meetings?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who were those officials?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Mr. Dokmanovic, Mr. Hadzic, and Mr. Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: If I could ask that 65 ter 6254 be shown again on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Before we go any further, Witness, can I ask you whether by Mr. Milutinovic you mean Mr. Milanovic when you speak of Mrgud?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes, Milanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how often did you see Milanovic in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He used to visit Arkan in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: How often did he visit Arkan? Did he visit him frequently?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Often.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you give me -- can you tell me whether it may have been once, twice a month or more?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Twice a month.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did Arkan behave towards Milanovic?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was arrogant towards him.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And do you know the purpose of Milanovic's visits to Arkan's training centre?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: If you can now look at the photograph in front of you. I would like to ask you how did the government ministers gain access to the Dvorac? On the card in front of you, can you draw a line on the access road to the Dvorac?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you now mark where Arkan's guards were positioned guarding the training camp. Can you mark those with Xs.

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I please ask that this exhibit be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter document 6254 marked for the second time in court shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1010. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, you've just marked on the photograph the positions of the guards as the government ministers accessed the Dvorac. Did government ministers have to pass through the training camp to get to Dvorac?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No. There was a separate road that led to Dvorac and another one that led to Arkan's camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Did government ministers have to pass through Arkan's soldiers in order to get to the Dvorac?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes. They had to go through the line-up of his guards, among his guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And was there any division or any dividing line between Arkan's camp and the Dvorac?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Well, only that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And was the Dvorac and Arkan's camp all within the one compound?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: If I can now ask that 65 ter 4813.1, that's tab 17, be shown. Mr. President, my Case Manager has asked me to inform you that 65 ter 4879.1, 4879.2, and 4809.5 have now had their transcripts uploaded to e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. So we can lift MFI status.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, I would now like to look at a number of photographs of individuals, the first of which is in front of you. Do you recognise the man in this photograph, or both men in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I recognise both. Mr. Zeljko Raznjatovic and Mirko Siz.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I now ask that this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1011. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I next ask that 65 ter 4795.2, that's at tab 23, be shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the man in the picture in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Who is this man?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Arkan's colonel, Milorad Ulemek.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how do you recognise this Colonel Milorad Ulemek?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was also in the centre, in Arkan's training centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I now ask that this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1012. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I next ask that 65 ter 4774.2 be shown. That's at tab 27.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the man in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Who is this man?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Ulemek, also known as Legija.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I please ask that this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could you please ask the witness who Ulemek is.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, who is Ulemek, or otherwise known as Legija?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was a soldier, one of the trainers who trained Arkan's army.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What was his relationship to Arkan?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was one of his officers in charge of training. He trained the troops who were to be sent to the front line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1013. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, other than those soldiers who you've already identified as Arkan's men, are there other individuals who you recall that you saw at Erdut who served in Arkan's unit?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: There were a lot of them. Some I do remember, but you will have to show me photos. Otherwise, I won't be able to recall them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I ask that 65 ter 02343.1 be shown on the screen. This, Mr. President, is not on the Prosecution's 65 ter list. It was a document produced in proofing by the witness. And can this be -- can we go into private session as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise any individuals in the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan; and Mr. Pelevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What is Mr. Pelevic wearing in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Smoking, a tuxedo.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who was Mr. Pelevic?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic was Arkan's man in charge of training his troops in judo, karate, and now I think he's a politician. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And did you see him at the training centre in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Might I ask that this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1014. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I ask that 65 ter 4798.1 be shown. That's tab 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, in the photograph in front of you, do you recognise any of the men?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Who do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The first on the right is Mr. Slobodan Novakovic, also known as Cope. He was Arkan's general.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone else in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how do you recognise Mr. Cope? How do you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Because I saw him in the centre. He would sometimes come to the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I asked that this be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1015. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I now ask that 65 ter 4795.1, that's tab 22, be shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the man on the far left of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was Arkan's soldier. His name is Marinac.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how do you recognise him? Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: At the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And the man in the centre of this photograph, who is that?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I think that this is Zeljko Raznjatovic. I believe that's him.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: May I ask that this document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1016. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I ask that 65 ter 4752.2 be shown. That's tab 31.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise either of the men in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The gentleman at the front of this photo was known as Kaljavi.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how do you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was in my house looking for my husband.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can I please ask that this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Shouldn't we ask the witness whether this was one of Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, was this soldier part of Arkan's men, one of Arkan's soldiers?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He was one of the officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit Number P1017. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, you have identified a number of officers, Arkan's officers, who -- who -- from these photographs. Where did Arkan's officers live in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: At first they lived in the centre, and then some of them continued to live in private houses in Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who owned those private houses in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And how did Arkan's men and officers furnish those houses? Where did they get their furniture from?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They found some on the spot, and the rest they brought in.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Where did they bring the furniture from?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: From Bijeljina and Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Do you know whether they bought the furniture in Bijeljina and Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Where did they get the furniture from in -- from Bijeljina and Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: When you said that they didn't buy the furniture, where did they get the furniture from?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I don't know whether the furniture came from shops or whether they took it from some other private houses. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Dennehy, there's probably a misunderstanding. I see in the transcript your question being: "Do you know whether they bought the furniture..." The answer being "No," would mean that the witness doesn't know, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, did any looting take place in Erdut by Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Can you describe that looting for the Court?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They usually went into people's houses demanding money, and they also robbed the kiosk in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And whose houses did they demand money from?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Croat and Serb, both.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Did refugees arrive in Erdut during the war?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And where did those refugees live?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Abandoned Croat houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What do you know about the expulsions from Erdut in Easter 1992?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: People were rounded up in their homes, put on buses and taken somewhere between Osijek and Sarvas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Dennehy, I'm sorry, but it's more than time for the second break. Can we do that now? Witness -- first of all, closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Witness, before the break I asked you about the looting that took place in Erdut by Arkan's men, and you said that they -- Arkan's men demanded money from both Croat and Serb people. How did Arkan respond when he learned that his soldiers took money from Serbs in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He punished them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: What did he do to punish them?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He beat them. They beat them up and locked them up in the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And why did he beat them up?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: He wanted discipline, and he said these things couldn't be done without his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Now, before the break I also asked you about the expulsions from -- of Croats from Erdut in Easter 1992. You said that people were rounded up and put on buses. Who were the people that were rounded up in Easter 1992 from Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Croats and some Hungarians.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Were any Serbs expelled from Erdut in Easter 1992?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: And who put the Croats and Hungarians on the buses in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Men in camouflage uniforms and wearing masks on their faces. Military camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Do you know who those men were?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Do you know who was responsible for the expulsions?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Were any of Arkan's men involved in the expulsions?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. That concludes my questions for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, madam. I will not address you by name in view of your protective measures. My name is Zoran Zivanovic, and in these proceedings I represent Mr. Goran Hadzic. I will put to you a few questions regarding the evidence you have given. First of all, concerning the part where you spoke about the bombing, although I believe it was the shelling of the water supply system, would you tell me, do you know why it was precisely the water supply system that was shelled, that was targeted by this attack?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The soldiers of the Home Guards of Croatia were located there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. It is a worthwhile clarification. You have said that, among others, your husband was a victim of cruel treatment by Arkan and his men. Do you know what those allegations against him were based on? Who started all this business against your husband?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Colonel Milorad Stricevic told me that he had a document from local residents to the effect that my husband was an Ustasha.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And only because of that he was locked up and subjected to that interrogation and the beating. Did they ask anything from him?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I think we have to go to -- into private session, and we have to redact that last question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- are you able to tell whether what you saw was a press conference, a cabinet session, or something else?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: One of those was a press conference, and the other one was a cabinet session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain which one was a press conference and which one was a cabinet session, and how did you come to the conclusion which was which?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic made a speech after coming back from The Hague. He addressed journalists and reporters, telling them about these discussions concerning the survival of Serbs in that Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And in the other situation what was going on?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: In the second clip there were his ministers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise those ministers?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who they were?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: There was Mr. Mrgud and Mr. Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The clip shown you by the Prosecution? Just now while you were giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes. During my testimony, I saw the press conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I see. That's the reason I asked you. I'm asking you only about those two video-clips shown you by the Prosecutor showing Goran Hadzic. I'm asking about them. Those were both press conferences; right?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you saw Dokmanovic and Milanovic Mrgud in some other video-clip that has not been shown here today.

utterances.speaker: GH-101
