utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You have described how Arkan punished his own soldiers for various disciplinary infractions, violations, et cetera, and just now towards the end you spoke about the robbing of a kiosk in the village. Why was that kiosk so important that they should steal something from there? What did they steal?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Cigarettes and whatever money there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And that was stolen by members of that Arkan's unit?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were they punished for that? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the way you described, in the same way?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And could you just explain, because the Prosecutor asked you about it, you confirmed that he meted out punishment for robberies against Serbs. Did he punish people for kinds of robberies because they were committed without any orders, without any sense, or only if it concerned Serbian property?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Generally if it was done while he was absent from the centre. He punished people if they had committed robberies when he was away.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That means if they robbed Serbs and non-Serbs. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: I don't know about non-Serbs, but I know that he punished them for robbing Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Redirect, Ms. Dennehy?

utterances.speaker: MS. DENNEHY
utterances.text: I also have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, this -- oh, I'm sorry. I should first ask my colleagues whether they have any questions. Judge Mindua.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness. I have one or two questions for you. My first question is transcript page 56, lines 17 through 24. The Prosecutor asked you who were the men who put the Croats and the Hungarians on buses in Erdut, and you said those were men in uniforms, in camouflage uniforms, wearing masks on their faces. And there was another question, whether there were Arkan's soldiers among those men dressed in camouflage uniform, and you said, no, there were no Arkan's men. How do you know that there were no Arkan's men among those who wore camouflage uniforms and wore masks?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: The people who were on the buses who had returned home believed that no Arkan's men were among those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. There was another question from the Prosecutor, page 35, line 1 and 2. You said there were Hungarians who were detained and who were at some point forced to sing the Serbian anthem, and they stayed locked up for eight days and later they were gone. You don't know what became of them. And then later you said they were all dead. How do you know they were dead?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: Because there was an exhumation later, and those people were identified among those killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Now I understand. And my last question: You have described the weapons carried by Arkan's men. That was on page 16, lines 14 through 16. I know that you were able to describe those weapons very well. Do you have some knowledge of weapons?

utterances.speaker: GH-101
utterances.text: They told us themselves in talking amongst them what kind of weapons they were carrying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. It is very clear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Witness, I have one small question for you myself. Could we go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ma'am, this brings your testimony to an end. We thank you for coming to assist the Tribunal. You're now released as a witness. We wish you -- we wish you a safe journey back home. The court usher will escort you out of court after we go into closed session. Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stringer, do we have another witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no, Mr. President. This witness and also the previous witness, the cross-examinations were concluded earlier than previewed, and so we have just received the next witness into the building. She travelled today. So she will be ready for Thursday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So we will resume at 9.00, Thursday morning. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
